title: Parenting
definition: Parenting is the God-given responsibility of raising children with love, instruction, discipline, prayer, and dependence on the Lord.
summary: Parents are called to nurture, teach, discipline, and shepherd children toward the Lord.
christFocus: Jesus welcomes children, displays perfect compassion, and calls parents to reflect the Father's love, truth, patience, and care.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Parenting is stewardship. Children belong ultimately to God, and parents are entrusted with the responsibility to love, nurture, instruct, discipline, protect, and guide them.

Biblical parenting is not harsh control or passive neglect. It involves truth and tenderness, correction and encouragement, structure and compassion. Parents are called to teach the ways of the Lord both through words and through example.

Parents are limited and need grace. Their hope is not in perfect methods but in the mercy of God, the power of prayer, the wisdom of Scripture, and the saving work of Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Parents can feel overwhelmed, guilty, or unsure of how to lead their children. This doctrine matters because it reminds them that parenting is a God-given calling that must be carried out with grace, truth, humility, and dependence.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Teach Scripture naturally, pray consistently, discipline with love rather than anger, and model repentance when you fail. Ask God to help you shepherd the heart, not merely control behavior.
